name: Kiwi - Teams replies to requester
execution: Reject the sentinel or future ActivationCutoffUtc before reading any tickets
Run cutoff and ticket-page checks as top-level preflights rather than ancestor containers
Read at most 51 mapped ticket roots and fail before processing if 51 are returned
Read replies with Teams Graph through the Teams connector using top=50
Fail before processing a reply page when @odata.nextLink exists or 50 replies are returned
Ignore replies older than ActivationCutoffUtc and messages without a non-empty human from.user.id
Ignore application/system/root messages
Skip every SourceMessageId already present in TicketExchanges
Resolve the human author with Office 365 Users and require accountEnabled plus userPrincipalName
Read the SharePoint PeopleManager FirstName profile property and fail closed when it is absent
Ensure the SharePoint user and require effective EditListItems on the exact EuropaTickets item
Convert Teams HTML with Content Conversion before classification
Treat only literal case-sensitive @user followed by end, space, LF or CRLF as public
Record all other human replies once as Internal and never dispatch them
Reject empty or greater-than-255 public text visibly without truncation
Append LF, the verified FirstName profile value, LF and learn.IT; validate the complete signed text within 255 characters
Create the unique Processing exchange before staging requester fields
Reject a later public reply while the same ticket has a Processing or AwaitingNativeRule exchange
Re-read Assigned_x0020_toId and assign the responder with an ETag-protected MERGE only when it is empty
Preserve every existing assignee and fail rather than overwrite a concurrent assignment
Write signed TeamsReplyText and TeamsReplyAgent, then re-read requester, thread, text, agent and assignee
Re-read staged requester and agent through SharePoint REST lookup-ID fields because native GetItem omits Person Id values
Change only TeamsReplyDispatchToken after the re-read matches
Mark the exchange AwaitingNativeRule after the token update
Set serial failure variables inside loops and perform any Terminate only after the loops

failureSemantics.Processing: No token is known to have been committed. Inspect the failed run and ticket before any manual recovery.
failureSemantics.AwaitingNativeRule: The token changed and SharePoint accepted the update. Native rules are queued, not proven delivered.
failureSemantics.AgentConfirmed: The actual Teams agent received and checked the rule copy, then manually confirmed this exact exchange.
failureSemantics.FailedTerminal: Validation failed; the reply is not retried automatically.
failureSemantics.IgnoredInternal: The reply was recorded as internal and can never be promoted automatically.
failureSemantics.uncertainDispatch: Never delete or replay a Processing exchange until an operator verifies the ticket token and native-rule history.

invariants: The flow never sends Outlook or SMTP mail
The flow never excludes Laurent solely because he owns the connections
SourceMessageId is the durable unique dedupe key
All loops and trigger runs are serial
No historical reply can run with the packaged sentinel cutoff
No page is silently truncated; a thread with 50 or more replies blocks every future run until pagination is implemented or the mapping is retired
Terminate actions are never nested in Foreach actions
SetVariable values never reference the variable being assigned; first-failure guards prevent later overwrites
Numeric SharePoint identity fields are validated with greater(int(coalesce(value,0)),0), never empty(), because the cloud runtime rejects empty(Integer)
Staged requester and agent correlation uses REST Demandeur0Id and TeamsReplyAgentId, not absent IDs inside native SPListExpandedUser objects
Agent signatures use PeopleManager FirstName and never infer a first name from displayName or userPrincipalName
Assigned_x0020_to is set only from an unassigned ETag snapshot; a pre-existing or concurrent assignee is never overwritten
Native TicketExchanges CreateItem actions use item/Ticket/Id for the lookup and plain item/Source; REST filters continue to use the TicketId internal lookup-ID property
The deepest concrete action path has exactly eight control parents, within the Power Automate save limit
Queued native rules are never labelled delivered
